newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Postbank - no decision yet on flotation date.
newsitem.headline: German Postbank - no decision yet on flotation date.

text.p: No date was yet set for the flotation of Postbank, the banking arm of the German postal authority, the bank said at the weekend, amid reports that the flotation could be threatened by massive provision costs.
An advance report in the news magazine Spiegel said that the Postbank flotation was under threat as the group would report provisions of 1.554 million marks in its as-yet-unpublished 1996 accounts.

The provisions relate to payments which Postbank will be required to make to Post AG for the use of the post office's counter space to distribute its services. Postbank does not have its own network of branch offices.
This would lead to a loss of 1.2 billion marks in 1996 compared to profits of 300 million marks the previous year, Spiegel said, citing a secret internal document.

Postbank told Reuters that no date had yet been set for the bank's flotation and said that the Postbank board would decide whether it would sign a disputed co-operation agreement with the German post office, or Post AG.
He said the Postbank supervisory board would discuss the co-operation agreement, which was drafted by the German postal minister Wolfgang Boetsch, at a meeting on Wednesday.
A date for the bank's flotation could only be set after the signing of the agreement, the spokesman said.

An advance copy of Monday's Platow Brief newsletter said that the chairman of Postbank, Guenter Schneider, planned to tell a supervisory board on April 30 of his intentions to push for a flotation in 1997.
